_about: Host tool names the orchestration meter needs (sisi/orchestration.py). Per host: `delegation` tools start a worker (where the call carries the model and the brief text, as dotted paths into the tool's input); `exempt` tools are never counted as direct work (the question dialog, planning and to-do tools, messaging tools). Any other tool, including one named nowhere here, counts. `refuse` says how the host's before-tool hook refuses a call: `json-deny` prints the host's permission-deny JSON, `exit-2` exits with status 2 and the reason on standard error, `none` means the meter only counts there. `evidence` says how sure this entry is. A delegation entry's name may be a shell-style pattern (`*delegate_task`). `async` says how the tool's result marks a background launch: the dotted `path` into the result, the `running` values meaning "still running", and the `ids` paths whose values the later completion message will carry; `title` is the input path of the task's title, the other way that message names it. A listed tool with no `async` is a launch when its call returned in under five seconds with no report in the result.
